definitions.definition: The study of God's character using the laws of physics as evidence.
definitions.example: Like using fingerprints to identify a person, theophysics uses physical laws to describe God.

definitions.definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system; things naturally tend to become more disordered over time.
definitions.example: Your messy bedroom naturally gets messier without you cleaning it.

definitions.definition: A mathematical table of numbers that shows how different variables are connected to each other in a system.
definitions.example: Like a spreadsheet that shows how much each friend influences every other friend in a group.

definitions.definition: Numbers that measure how strongly two forces or particles interact with each other.
definitions.example: Like a rating of how tightly two magnets stick together.

definitions.definition: Equations that describe how things change continuously over time or space.
definitions.example: Like a formula that predicts how fast a cup of coffee cools down every minute.

definitions.definition: Travels or spreads through space.
definitions.example: Sound propagates through air from a speaker to your ear.

definitions.definition: A substance or material that a wave travels through, like air, water, or glass.
definitions.example: Air is the medium for sound waves; water is the medium for ocean waves.

definitions.definition: A tiny particle of light that carries electromagnetic energy.
definitions.example: A photon is like a single bullet of light from a flashlight.

definitions.definition: The light-sensitive layer at the back of your eye that detects images.
definitions.example: The retina is like the film in a camera that captures the picture.

definitions.definition: A set of four fundamental laws that describe how electricity and magnetism work and how light is made.
definitions.example: They are like the instruction manual for how electric and magnetic fields create each other.

definitions.definition: Einstein's famous equation showing that a tiny amount of mass can be converted into a huge amount of energy.
definitions.example: A single raisin has enough hidden energy to power a city for a day.

definitions.definition: Not moving or not able to react chemically; seeming lifeless or inactive.
definitions.example: A rock sitting on the ground looks inert, but it contains atoms with huge energy.

definitions.definition: Size, amount, or importance of something.
definitions.example: The magnitude of an earthquake tells you how strong it is.

definitions.definition: A system that does not exchange energy or matter with anything outside it.
definitions.example: A sealed thermos of hot coffee is a closed system—no heat or steam escapes.

definitions.definition: The one-way direction of time from past to future, linked to increasing disorder.
definitions.example: You can't un-break an egg because the arrow of time only goes forward.

definitions.definition: A rule that says erasing information always requires a tiny amount of energy, so the universe keeps a record.
definitions.example: Like shredding a document—it takes energy, and the pieces still exist somewhere.

definitions.definition: The law of thermodynamics that says disorder in a closed system always increases over time.
definitions.example: Your room gets messier on its own, but never cleaner without you working.

definitions.definition: Claude Shannon, a scientist who created information theory and defined the maximum rate of error-free data transmission.
definitions.example: He figured out the fastest speed you can send a text message without mistakes.

definitions.definition: Andrey Kolmogorov, a mathematician who defined the shortest possible computer program that can produce a given output.
definitions.example: The shortest set of instructions to draw a picture of a tree.

definitions.definition: A condition of high order and low disorder, like a perfectly organized room.
definitions.example: The early universe was in a low-entropy state, like a brand-new deck of cards in perfect order.

definitions.definition: Converting information into a specific format for storage or transmission.
definitions.example: Turning a song into MP3 format is encoding.

definitions.definition: The maximum amount of information that can be sent through a communication link without errors.
definitions.example: The maximum number of text messages you can send per second through a fiber optic cable.

definitions.definition: A Greek word meaning 'word,' 'reason,' or 'principle'; in theology, it refers to Jesus as the divine Word of God.
definitions.example: In the Bible, John says 'In the beginning was the Word (Logos), and the Word was with God.'

definitions.definition: A point of view from which you measure motion, time, and space; different frames can see different things.
definitions.example: From a train, the trees seem to move backward; from the ground, the train moves forward.

definitions.definition: A mathematical value that stays the same for all observers, combining both space and time measurements.
definitions.example: Even if two people disagree on how long or far something is, they agree on the spacetime interval.

definitions.definition: Something that does not change, no matter how you measure it or from where.
definitions.example: The number of sides of a square is invariant—it's always four.

definitions.definition: The idea that gravity and acceleration feel exactly the same; you can't tell them apart in a sealed room.
definitions.example: In an elevator accelerating upward, you feel heavier—just like stronger gravity.

definitions.definition: A quantum state where a particle exists in all possible states at once until it is measured.
definitions.example: Like a spinning coin that is both heads and tails until you catch it.

definitions.definition: In quantum physics, the act of measuring or interacting with a particle, which forces it to pick one state.
definitions.example: Looking at the spinning coin forces it to land on heads or tails.

definitions.definition: When a quantum particle's many possible states suddenly become just one real state due to measurement.
definitions.example: The cloud of possibilities collapses into a single actual outcome.

definitions.definition: Two particles that are linked so that measuring one instantly affects the other, no matter how far apart they are.
definitions.example: Like two magic coins that always show the same side, even if one is on Earth and the other on Mars.

definitions.definition: The exact location of a particle in space.
definitions.example: Where a marble is on a table is its position.

definitions.definition: The mass of an object multiplied by its speed; a measure of how hard it is to stop something moving.
definitions.example: A fast truck has more momentum than a slow bicycle.

definitions.definition: The process where an unstable atom changes into a different atom by releasing particles and energy.
definitions.example: Uranium slowly turns into lead over billions of years.

definitions.definition: A particle in the nucleus of an atom that has no electric charge.
definitions.example: Neutrons are like neutral glue that help hold the nucleus together.

definitions.definition: A positively charged particle in the nucleus of an atom.
definitions.example: The number of protons determines what element an atom is.

definitions.definition: A tiny, nearly massless particle that rarely interacts with matter.
definitions.example: Trillions of neutrinos from the sun pass through your body every second without you noticing.

definitions.definition: Cannot be undone or changed back to the original state.
definitions.example: Baking a cake is irreversible—you can't turn it back into batter.

definitions.definition: The dense, central core of an atom, made of protons and neutrons.
definitions.example: The nucleus is like the sun in the center of the solar system of electrons.

definitions.definition: A sacred promise or agreement between God and people.
definitions.example: In the Bible, God made a covenant with Noah to never flood the whole earth again.

definitions.definition: When waves are perfectly aligned, all moving together in step, creating a strong combined effect.
definitions.example: A laser beam is coherent light—all the light waves march together like soldiers.

definitions.definition: When two waves have their peaks and valleys at the same time, so they add up.
definitions.example: Two people pushing a swing at the exact same moment are in phase.

definitions.definition: When waves combine to make a bigger wave because they are aligned.
definitions.example: Two ripples in a pond meeting to form a bigger ripple.

definitions.definition: The process where a quantum system loses its special quantum properties by interacting with the environment.
definitions.example: Like a spinning coin slowing down and falling flat, losing its 'both sides' magic.

definitions.definition: A mathematical equation that describes how a system changes over time, including all influences.
definitions.example: Like a recipe that predicts how a whole ecosystem will evolve.

definitions.definition: A mathematical operation that adds up tiny pieces to find a total, like area under a curve.
definitions.example: Adding up all the slices of pizza to find the total amount of pizza.

definitions.definition: Lack of balance or symmetry; one side is different from the other.
definitions.example: A haircut that is longer on one side than the other has asymmetry.

definitions.definition: Growing extremely fast because each step multiplies the previous amount.
definitions.example: A virus spreading where each person infects two more, who each infect two more, grows exponentially.

definitions.definition: A mathematical term that represents the ability to make choices or changes in a system.
definitions.example: In a video game, a 'freedom variable' would be how many different paths you can choose.

definitions.definition: A symbolic equation where chi (χ) equals coherence (C), representing the final unified state.
definitions.example: Like writing 'Total = Everything aligned' as a math formula.

definitions.definition: Obvious without needing proof or explanation.
definitions.example: That the sun is bright is self-evident when you look at it.
